title: TESS full-frame light curves of 33,881 old M dwarfs leave contraction-only CPV rates allowed (3 seen, 6.4 predicted with 2-minute data); the old candidates have one narrow dip, unlike young CPVs
abstract: Complex periodic variables (CPVs) are young, fast-rotating M dwarfs with sharp dips at the rotation period. A frozen contraction-only (x-only) model predicts CPVs among old main-sequence M dwarfs at the corotation-to-stellar radius ratio x of young hosts. We built an independent sample from TESS-SPOC full-frame light curves (200-s cadence, sectors 56-86) of 33,881 old M dwarfs without 2-minute data. A partial-read period screen (97-99% complete), the source pipeline, centroid source location, eRASS1 X-ray data and blind labels with calibration stars gave 327 old rapid rotators. Only 7 of 20 signals at P < 0.2 d are on target; X-ray data agree (saturated probability 0.79 on target, 0.28 off target). Among 82 on-target stars in the model x range, the model predicts 1.26 CPVs (0.88-1.80) and we observe 1. With the 2-minute result of an earlier publication, 3 CPVs are seen for 6.36 (4.10-9.88) predicted, p = 0.15. The main-sequence rate factor at fixed x is 0.46 (0.11-1.34). Thus contraction alone remains allowed, but strong suppression is excluded. All three old candidates are doubtful: two show one narrow dip and one is a probable eclipsing binary. All 126 on-target young-sample CPVs have two or more dips. A rule that counts only curves with two or more dips gives p = 0.02 or 0.003, but we chose this rule after inspection. Limitations: small numbers, labels from one automated vetter, efficiency from 2-minute injections, and published aggregate numbers for the 2-minute part.
